webafx-mailer API Reference ​

This document is the complete reference for every public export of blendsdk/webafx-mailer: three classes, four factory functions, eight interfaces, and one constant. Everything is imported from the package root — the package ships a single ESM entry point with bundled type declarations.

Reading conventions

  • typescript fragment blocks contain declaration references (class shapes, function signatures). Plain typescript blocks are complete, runnable examples with all imports.
  • In property tables, an optional property carries a ? suffix (e.g. cc?), mirroring its TypeScript declaration.

Note — The plugin factory functions return PluginDefinition from blendsdk/webafx. That type is not re-exported by this package; import it from blendsdk/webafx (an optional peer dependency) if you need to annotate plugin values explicitly.

Exports at a Glance ​

SymbolKindDescription
MailProviderAbstract classBase contract for all mail backends: serviceName, send(), health(), shutdown().
SmtpMailProviderClassReal SMTP delivery through a nodemailer transport.
MemoryMailProviderClassIn-memory capture for development and testing, with assertion helpers.
SentMailEntryInterface (type-only){ message, result } record stored by MemoryMailProvider.
MailMessageInterface (type-only)Complete outgoing email (recipients, subject, bodies, attachments).
MailAttachmentInterface (type-only)Attachment with filename, content (Buffer or base64 string), and optional contentType.
MailResultInterface (type-only)Send outcome: accepted, rejected, and an optional messageId.
MailProviderConfigInterface (type-only)Base provider configuration carrying the optional serviceName.
SmtpMailConfigInterface (type-only)SMTP connection settings; extends MailProviderConfig.
MemoryMailConfigInterface (type-only)Memory backend configuration; extends MailProviderConfig with no extra fields.
MailFactoryConfigInterface (type-only)Type-discriminated configuration for createMailProvider().
createMailPluginFunctionAdapts any MailProvider into a WebAFX PluginDefinition.
smtpMailPluginFunctionOne-liner: creates an SMTP provider internally and returns its plugin.
memoryMailPluginFunctionOne-liner: creates an in-memory provider internally and returns its plugin.
createMailProviderFunctionBackend factory keyed by config.type ("smtp" or "memory").
DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAMEConstant"mailer" — default service name applied by every provider.

MailProvider (Abstract Base Class) ​

MailProvider is the abstract base every backend extends — the shipped SmtpMailProvider and MemoryMailProvider, plus any custom subclass you write. It defines the three-method contract (send, health, shutdown) and resolves the provider's service identity from MailProviderConfig: config.serviceName ?? DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME. Because the class is abstract it cannot be instantiated directly — construct a concrete subclass instead. Custom subclasses are fully supported by createMailPlugin().

typescript
abstract class MailProvider {
    protected _serviceName: string;

    constructor(config: MailProviderConfig);

    get serviceName(): string;

    abstract send(message: MailMessage): Promise<MailResult>;
    abstract health(): Promise<boolean>;
    abstract shutdown(): Promise<void>;
}

Constructor ​

constructor(config: MailProviderConfig)

ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configMailProviderConfigYes—Base configuration. config.serviceName is stored in _serviceName, defaulting to "mailer".

Properties ​

PropertyTypeDescription
_serviceNameprotected stringBacking field holding the resolved service name.
serviceNamestring (getter, read-only)Service-container registration name used when the provider is registered as a WebAFX singleton service.

Methods ​

MethodSignatureReturnsDescription
sendabstract send(message: MailMessage): Promise<MailResult>Promise<MailResult>Sends an email message. Resolves with accepted/rejected recipients and the server-assigned message ID; throws when sending fails (connection issues, auth failures, etc.).
healthabstract health(): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>Health check — resolves to true when the backend is operational. SMTP verifies the transport connection via EHLO/HELO; Memory always returns true.
shutdownabstract shutdown(): Promise<void>Promise<void>Graceful shutdown — closes connections and releases resources. SMTP closes the nodemailer transport and connection pool; Memory clears all stored messages.

Example ​

Implementing the contract with a minimal custom backend:

typescript
import {
    MailProvider,
    type MailMessage,
    type MailProviderConfig,
    type MailResult,
} from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

/** Minimal custom backend that logs messages instead of delivering them. */
class ConsoleMailProvider extends MailProvider {
    constructor(config: MailProviderConfig = {}) {
        super(config);
    }

    async send(message: MailMessage): Promise<MailResult> {
        const recipients = Array.isArray(message.to) ? message.to : [message.to];
        console.log(`[console-mail] "${message.subject}" -> ${recipients.join(", ")}`);

        return {
            accepted: recipients,
            rejected: [],
            messageId: `<console-${Date.now()}@local>`,
        };
    }

    async health(): Promise<boolean> {
        return true;
    }

    async shutdown(): Promise<void> {
        console.log("[console-mail] transport closed");
    }
}

const mailer: MailProvider = new ConsoleMailProvider({ serviceName: "audit-mailer" });

console.log(mailer.serviceName);    // "audit-mailer"
console.log(await mailer.health()); // true

const result = await mailer.send({
    from: "noreply@example.com",
    to: ["ops@example.com", "oncall@example.com"],
    subject: "Deployment finished",
    text: "Deployment #42 completed successfully.",
});

console.log(result.accepted); // ["ops@example.com", "oncall@example.com"]
console.log(result.rejected); // []

await mailer.shutdown();

SmtpMailProvider ​

Concrete backend that delivers real email through nodemailer. The constructor builds one nodemailer transport from SmtpMailConfig; secure defaults to false (STARTTLS on port 587) and TLS certificate validation stays configurable through the tls option — there is no hardcoded rejectUnauthorized: false. send() maps MailMessage to nodemailer's format and back into a MailResult, health() runs transporter.verify(), and shutdown() closes the transport's connection pool.

typescript
class SmtpMailProvider extends MailProvider {
    // Transport type from the "nodemailer" package
    protected transporter: nodemailer.Transporter;

    constructor(config: SmtpMailConfig);

    send(message: MailMessage): Promise<MailResult>;
    health(): Promise<boolean>;
    shutdown(): Promise<void>;
}

Constructor ​

constructor(config: SmtpMailConfig)

ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configSmtpMailConfigYes—SMTP connection settings (host, port, optional secure, auth, tls, serviceName); used once to create the nodemailer transport.

Properties ​

PropertyTypeDescription
transporterprotected nodemailer.TransporterNodemailer transport instance — handles SMTP connection pooling internally.
serviceNamestring (getter, read-only)Inherited from MailProvider; equals config.serviceName ?? "mailer".

Methods ​

MethodSignatureReturnsDescription
sendsend(message: MailMessage): Promise<MailResult>Promise<MailResult>Translates the message into nodemailer's sendMail format — array to/cc/bcc recipients are joined with ", ", attachments are mapped to { filename, content, contentType } — sends it, and maps the response into a MailResult (accepted/rejected stringified, messageId passed through). Throws on SMTP connection failure, authentication failure, or send rejection.
healthhealth(): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>Runs transporter.verify() — an EHLO/HELO handshake with the server that sends no email. Resolves to false on any failure; never throws.
shutdownshutdown(): Promise<void>Promise<void>Calls transporter.close(), releasing the underlying TCP connection pool. Subsequent send() calls fail.

Example ​

typescript
import { SmtpMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "smtp.example.com",
    port: 587,
    secure: false, // STARTTLS — use true for implicit TLS (typically port 465)
    auth: {
        user: "user@example.com",
        pass: "secret",
    },
});

console.log("Reachable:", await mailer.health());

try {
    const result = await mailer.send({
        from: "noreply@example.com",
        to: "customer@example.com",
        subject: "Your receipt",
        text: "Thanks for your purchase.",
        html: "<p>Thanks for your purchase.</p>",
    });

    console.log("Accepted:", result.accepted);
    console.log("Message ID:", result.messageId);
} catch (error) {
    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "SMTP send failed";
    console.error("Send failed:", reason);
} finally {
    await mailer.shutdown();
}

MemoryMailProvider ​

Test-oriented backend that never sends anything: each send() stores the message and its result as a SentMailEntry ({ message, result }) in an internal array, and the class exposes assertion helpers — getSentMessages(), getLastMessage(), and clear(). Recipients are normalized from single strings or arrays; every to + cc + bcc address lands in accepted, rejected is always [], and messageId follows the deterministic pattern <memory-<timestamp>-<index>@test> (where index is the store length at send time, so consecutive sends stay unique).

typescript
class MemoryMailProvider extends MailProvider {
    protected messages: SentMailEntry[];

    constructor(config?: MemoryMailConfig);

    send(message: MailMessage): Promise<MailResult>;
    getSentMessages(): SentMailEntry[];
    getLastMessage(): SentMailEntry | undefined;
    clear(): void;
    health(): Promise<boolean>;
    shutdown(): Promise<void>;
}

Constructor ​

constructor(config?: MemoryMailConfig)

ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configMemoryMailConfigNo{}Optional configuration; only serviceName is meaningful. Defaults to an empty config (serviceName resolves to "mailer").

Properties ​

PropertyTypeDescription
messagesprotected SentMailEntry[]Internal store of all captured messages and their results; starts empty.
serviceNamestring (getter, read-only)Inherited from MailProvider; equals config.serviceName ?? "mailer".

Methods ​

MethodSignatureReturnsDescription
sendsend(message: MailMessage): Promise<MailResult>Promise<MailResult>Stores the message; cannot fail under normal operation. All to + cc + bcc recipients (normalized to arrays) are returned in accepted, in that order; rejected is always []; messageId is <memory-<timestamp>-<index>@test>.
getSentMessagesgetSentMessages(): SentMailEntry[]SentMailEntry[]Returns a shallow copy of the internal store in send order — mutating the returned array does not affect the provider's state. Entries inside the copy are shared references.
getLastMessagegetLastMessage(): SentMailEntry | undefinedSentMailEntry | undefinedReturns the most recently sent entry, or undefined when no messages have been sent.
clearclear(): voidvoidEmpties the store. Useful for resetting state between test cases.
healthhealth(): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>Always resolves to true — the in-memory backend has no external dependencies.
shutdownshutdown(): Promise<void>Promise<void>Clears all stored messages (delegates to clear()), aligning teardown with the shared MailProvider lifecycle.

Example ​

typescript
import { MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider({ serviceName: "test-mailer" });

const result = await mailer.send({
    from: "noreply@example.com",
    to: "new-user@example.com",
    cc: "team@example.com",
    subject: "Welcome!",
    text: "Welcome aboard!",
});

console.log(result.accepted);  // ["new-user@example.com", "team@example.com"]
console.log(result.rejected);  // []
console.log(result.messageId); // "<memory-…@test>"

const last = mailer.getLastMessage();
console.log(last?.message.subject);           // "Welcome!"
console.log(mailer.getSentMessages().length); // 1

mailer.clear();
console.log(mailer.getSentMessages().length); // 0

await mailer.shutdown();

Plugin Factory Functions ​

The WebAFX integration layer. These functions produce a PluginDefinition and are the only part of the package that depends on blendsdk/webafx — the providers themselves are fully usable standalone. Every definition returned by createMailPlugin() (and therefore by the one-liners) is populated as follows:

  • name — provider.serviceName.
  • priority — options?.priority ?? 30; lower values install earlier, and 0 is a valid priority.
  • factory — an async function receiving the WebAFX plugin context ({ app, logger }). It registers the provider as a singleton service (factory: () => provider) with a dispose hook that awaits provider.shutdown(), logs Mail plugin "<serviceName>" initialized (<ClassName>) through the context logger, and returns { health, shutdown } hooks bridged to the provider.

createMailPlugin ​

typescript
function createMailPlugin(
    provider: MailProvider,
    options?: { priority?: number }
): PluginDefinition;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
providerMailProviderYes—Any MailProvider instance — SMTP, memory, or a custom subclass.
options{ priority?: number }NoundefinedOptional overrides for the produced plugin.
options.prioritynumberNo30Plugin priority; lower values install earlier. 0 is valid.

Returns — PluginDefinition (from blendsdk/webafx), configured as described above. The provider instance is captured by reference, so the plugin always resolves the same object.

typescript
import { createMailPlugin, MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider({ serviceName: "transactional-mailer" });
const plugin = createMailPlugin(mailer, { priority: 10 });

console.log(plugin.name);           // "transactional-mailer"
console.log(plugin.priority);       // 10
console.log(typeof plugin.factory); // "function"

await mailer.shutdown();

smtpMailPlugin ​

typescript
function smtpMailPlugin(config: SmtpMailConfig): PluginDefinition;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configSmtpMailConfigYes—SMTP settings used internally as new SmtpMailProvider(config) before delegating to createMailPlugin().

Returns — PluginDefinition. The SmtpMailProvider is created internally and owned by the plugin; it is shut down through the plugin's shutdown hook when the application disposes its services.

typescript
import { smtpMailPlugin } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const plugin = smtpMailPlugin({
    host: "smtp.example.com",
    port: 587,
    secure: false,
    auth: { user: "user@example.com", pass: "secret" },
});

console.log(plugin.name);     // "mailer" (provider service name)
console.log(plugin.priority); // 30 (default plugin priority)

Typical registration inside a WebAFX application:

typescript
// WebAFX application bootstrap
app.use(smtpMailPlugin({
    host: "smtp.example.com",
    port: 587,
    secure: false,
    auth: { user: "user@example.com", pass: "secret" },
}));

memoryMailPlugin ​

typescript
function memoryMailPlugin(config?: MemoryMailConfig): PluginDefinition;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configMemoryMailConfigNoundefined (the provider defaults to {})Optional service-name override for the internally created MemoryMailProvider.

Returns — PluginDefinition. The provider instance stays internal to the plugin — when a test needs to assert on getSentMessages(), create the MemoryMailProvider yourself and pass it to createMailPlugin() instead.

typescript
import { memoryMailPlugin } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const plugin = memoryMailPlugin();                         // serviceName "mailer"
const named = memoryMailPlugin({ serviceName: "dev-mailer" });

console.log(plugin.name); // "mailer"
console.log(named.name);  // "dev-mailer"

createMailProvider ​

typescript
function createMailProvider(config: MailFactoryConfig): MailProvider;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configMailFactoryConfigYes—Type-discriminated configuration; config.type selects the backend.

Returns — MailProvider:

  • type: "smtp" → a SmtpMailProvider built from serviceName, host, port, secure, auth, and tls.
  • type: "memory" → a MemoryMailProvider built from serviceName only.

Throws — Error when config.type is neither "smtp" nor "memory": Unknown mail type: "<value>". Supported types: "smtp", "memory". This is a runtime guard for untyped or environment-provided configuration that TypeScript could not check at compile time.

typescript
import {
    createMailProvider,
    MemoryMailProvider,
    SmtpMailProvider,
    type MailFactoryConfig,
} from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

// Environment-based backend switching:
const config: MailFactoryConfig = {
    type: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" ? "smtp" : "memory",
    serviceName: "transactional-mailer",
    host: process.env.SMTP_HOST ?? "localhost",
    port: Number(process.env.SMTP_PORT ?? "587"),
};

const mailer = createMailProvider(config);

console.log(mailer instanceof SmtpMailProvider);   // true in production
console.log(mailer instanceof MemoryMailProvider); // true otherwise
console.log(mailer.serviceName);                   // "transactional-mailer"

// Unknown types fail fast with a descriptive error:
try {
    createMailProvider({ type: "sendgrid" as "smtp" });
} catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "unexpected error";
    console.log(message);
    // Unknown mail type: "sendgrid". Supported types: "smtp", "memory".
}

await mailer.shutdown();

Message Types ​

MailMessage ​

Complete description of an outgoing email. At least one of text or html should be provided for body content.

PropertyTypeDescription
fromstringSender email address (e.g. "noreply@example.com" or "Name <email>"). Required.
tostring | string[]Primary recipient(s) — a single address or an array of addresses. Required.
cc?string | string[]Carbon copy recipient(s). Optional.
bcc?string | string[]Blind carbon copy recipient(s). Optional.
subjectstringEmail subject line. Required.
text?stringPlain-text body — used as fallback when html is also provided.
html?stringHTML body — rich email content.
attachments?MailAttachment[]File attachments. Optional.

MailAttachment ​

A file to attach to an outgoing email.

PropertyTypeDescription
filenamestringFilename for the attachment (e.g. "report.pdf"). Required.
contentBuffer | stringAttachment content — a raw Buffer for binary data, or a base64-encoded string. Required.
contentType?stringMIME content type (e.g. "application/pdf", "text/plain"). Optional.

MailResult ​

Result of a send operation, as resolved by send() on every backend.

PropertyTypeDescription
acceptedstring[]Email addresses that accepted the message.
rejectedstring[]Email addresses that rejected the message; always [] for the memory backend.
messageId?stringMessage ID assigned by the mail server (e.g. "<abc123@smtp.example.com>"). The memory backend generates <memory-<timestamp>-<index>@test>. Optional.

SentMailEntry ​

Record stored by MemoryMailProvider for each captured message.

PropertyTypeDescription
messageMailMessageThe original mail message as submitted to send().
resultMailResultThe result returned from send().

Configuration Types ​

MailProviderConfig ​

Base configuration shared by all mail providers.

PropertyTypeDescription
serviceName?stringService name for WebAFX service container registration. Default: "mailer" (DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME). Use different names for multi-provider scenarios (e.g. "transactional-mailer", "marketing-mailer"). Optional.

SmtpMailConfig ​

Extends MailProviderConfig with all settings needed to connect to an SMTP server via nodemailer.

PropertyTypeDescription
hoststringSMTP server hostname (e.g. "smtp.example.com"). Required.
portnumberSMTP server port. Common values: 25, 465 (TLS), 587 (STARTTLS). Required.
secure?booleanUse a direct TLS connection. Default false — STARTTLS, typical for port 587; set true for implicit TLS (typically port 465). Optional.
auth?{ user: string; pass: string }SMTP authentication credentials — omit for unauthenticated servers. Optional.
tls?{ rejectUnauthorized?: boolean; [key: string]: unknown }Additional TLS options — certificate validation is configurable here. Optional.
serviceName?stringInherited from MailProviderConfig; default "mailer". Optional.

MemoryMailConfig ​

Extends MailProviderConfig and adds no additional fields — only serviceName is meaningful for the in-memory backend, which stores messages in memory for test assertions.

PropertyTypeDescription
serviceName?stringInherited from MailProviderConfig; default "mailer". Optional.

MailFactoryConfig ​

Type-discriminated configuration used by createMailProvider() for environment-based backend switching. The SMTP-specific fields are only read when type === "smtp".

PropertyTypeDescription
type"smtp" | "memory"Backend selector — determines which provider is created. Required.
serviceName?stringService name for WebAFX service container registration. Default: "mailer". Optional; passed through to the created provider.
host?stringSMTP server hostname. Used only when type is "smtp"; required at runtime for SMTP.
port?numberSMTP server port. Used only when type is "smtp"; required at runtime for SMTP.
secure?booleanUse a direct TLS connection. Forwarded to the SMTP provider. Optional.
auth?{ user: string; pass: string }SMTP authentication credentials. Forwarded to the SMTP provider. Optional.
tls?{ rejectUnauthorized?: boolean; [key: string]: unknown }Additional TLS options. Forwarded to the SMTP provider. Optional.

Constants ​

DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME ​

typescript
const DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME = "mailer";
NameTypeValueDescription
DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME"mailer" (string literal)"mailer"Default service name for mail when not specified in config. Applied by the MailProvider constructor as config.serviceName ?? DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME.
typescript
import { DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME, MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();

console.log(DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME); // "mailer"
console.log(mailer.serviceName);   // "mailer" — resolved from the default

See Also ​

  • Overview — what the package is, its architecture, and dependencies.
  • Core Concepts — deep dive into the provider contract, message model, backends, and plugin layer.
  • Basic Usage — task-oriented walkthroughs for sending email, testing, and WebAFX integration.

webafx-mailer Examples Library ​

A categorized collection of copy-paste ready examples covering every feature area of blendsdk/webafx-mailer — in-memory capture, real SMTP delivery, WebAFX plugin wiring, backend switching, testing, and custom providers. Every example is complete strict-mode TypeScript with full imports, ES modules, and top-level await (Node.js >= 22). SMTP examples target smtp.example.com placeholders — swap in real credentials; local SMTP examples target Mailpit on localhost:1025. Test examples additionally require Vitest.

Getting Started with the Memory Backend ​

The in-memory backend is the fastest way to send (and capture) email — no mail server, no network, no Docker.

Send Your First Email ​

Create a MemoryMailProvider and send a message; it is stored in process instead of being delivered.

typescript
import { MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();

const result = await mailer.send({
    from: "noreply@example.com",
    to: "user@example.com",
    subject: "Welcome!",
    text: "Welcome to our service!",
});

console.log("Accepted:", result.accepted);     // ["user@example.com"]
console.log("Rejected:", result.rejected);     // []
console.log("Message ID:", result.messageId);  // "<memory-...@test>" (timestamp + index)

const sent = mailer.getSentMessages();
console.log("Stored messages:", sent.length);            // 1
console.log("Stored subject:", sent[0].message.subject); // "Welcome!"

await mailer.shutdown();

Inspect Sent Messages ​

getSentMessages() returns a shallow copy of every captured SentMailEntry (message plus result); getLastMessage() is a shortcut to the most recent one.

typescript
import { MemoryMailProvider, type SentMailEntry } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();

await mailer.send({
    from: "noreply@example.com",
    to: "first@example.com",
    subject: "First",
    text: "First message",
});

await mailer.send({
    from: "noreply@example.com",
    to: "second@example.com",
    subject: "Second",
    text: "Second message",
});

const entries: SentMailEntry[] = mailer.getSentMessages();
console.log("Count:", entries.length);                      // 2
console.log("First subject:", entries[0].message.subject);  // "First"
console.log("Second subject:", entries[1].message.subject); // "Second"

const last = mailer.getLastMessage();
console.log("Last subject:", last?.message.subject);   // "Second"
console.log("Last accepted:", last?.result.accepted);  // ["second@example.com"]

// getSentMessages() returns a shallow copy — trimming it does not affect the store.
const copy = mailer.getSentMessages();
copy.length = 0;
console.log("Store still holds:", mailer.getSentMessages().length); // 2

await mailer.shutdown();

Clear and Reuse the Store ​

clear() empties the captured messages without recreating the provider — useful for resetting between scenarios.

typescript
import { MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();

await mailer.send({ from: "a@example.com", to: "b@example.com", subject: "One", text: "1" });
await mailer.send({ from: "a@example.com", to: "b@example.com", subject: "Two", text: "2" });

console.log(mailer.getSentMessages().length); // 2

mailer.clear();

console.log(mailer.getSentMessages().length); // 0
console.log(mailer.getLastMessage());         // undefined

// The provider remains fully usable after a clear.
await mailer.send({ from: "a@example.com", to: "b@example.com", subject: "Three", text: "3" });
console.log(mailer.getLastMessage()?.message.subject); // "Three"

await mailer.shutdown();

Sending Real Email over SMTP ​

Real delivery through nodemailer. All examples wrap send() in try/finally so the transport pool is always closed.

Send via SMTP with STARTTLS (Port 587) ​

The modern default: secure is false and the connection upgrades through STARTTLS.

typescript
import { SmtpMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "smtp.example.com",
    port: 587,
    secure: false, // STARTTLS — `secure` defaults to false; shown here explicitly
    auth: {
        user: "user@example.com",
        pass: "secret",
    },
});

try {
    const result = await mailer.send({
        from: "noreply@example.com",
        to: "customer@example.com",
        subject: "Your receipt",
        text: "Thanks for your purchase.",
    });

    console.log("Accepted:", result.accepted);    // ["customer@example.com"]
    console.log("Message ID:", result.messageId); // server-assigned, e.g. "<...@smtp.example.com>"
} catch (error) {
    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    console.error("SMTP send failed:", reason);
} finally {
    await mailer.shutdown();
}

Result: accepted lists the recipient and messageId is assigned by the SMTP server. Authentication or connection failures are thrown from send().

Send with Implicit TLS (Port 465) ​

Set secure: true for a direct TLS connection, conventionally on port 465.

typescript
import { SmtpMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "smtp.example.com",
    port: 465,
    secure: true, // implicit TLS — typically port 465
    auth: {
        user: "user@example.com",
        pass: "secret",
    },
});

try {
    const result = await mailer.send({
        from: "noreply@example.com",
        to: "customer@example.com",
        subject: "Secure delivery",
        text: "This message travels over an implicit TLS connection.",
    });

    console.log("Accepted:", result.accepted); // ["customer@example.com"]
} finally {
    await mailer.shutdown();
}

Send to a Local SMTP Server Without Authentication ​

Omit the auth block for development servers such as Mailpit that accept unauthenticated mail.

typescript
import { SmtpMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

// Start Mailpit locally with:
// docker-compose -p webafx-mailer -f ./docker/docker-compose.yml up -d
const mailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "localhost",
    port: 1025,
    secure: false,
});

try {
    const result = await mailer.send({
        from: "dev@example.com",
        to: "tester@example.com",
        subject: "Local delivery",
        text: "Inspect this message in the Mailpit web UI at http://localhost:8025",
    });

    console.log("Accepted:", result.accepted);    // ["tester@example.com"]
    console.log("Message ID:", result.messageId);
} finally {
    await mailer.shutdown();
}

Recipients and Content ​

Address shapes, CC/BCC, display names, HTML bodies, and attachments.

Send to Multiple Recipients ​

to accepts a single address or an array; every recipient is reported individually in the result.

typescript
import { MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();

const result = await mailer.send({
    from: "news@example.com",
    to: ["alice@example.com", "bob@example.com", "carol@example.com"],
    subject: "Release notes",
    text: "Version 2.0 is out.",
});

console.log(result.accepted);
// ["alice@example.com", "bob@example.com", "carol@example.com"]

await mailer.shutdown();

Use CC and BCC ​

cc and bcc follow the same single-or-array shape as to. On the memory backend, all of them appear in accepted.

typescript
import { MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();

const result = await mailer.send({
    from: "hr@example.com",
    to: "candidate@example.com",
    cc: ["hiring-manager@example.com", "recruiter@example.com"],
    bcc: "audit@example.com",
    subject: "Interview invitation",
    text: "We would like to invite you to an interview.",
});

console.log(result.accepted);
// ["candidate@example.com", "hiring-manager@example.com",
//  "recruiter@example.com", "audit@example.com"]

await mailer.shutdown();

Use Display Names in Addresses ​

from and recipient fields accept RFC 5322 display-name form ("Name <email>").

typescript
import { MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();

const result = await mailer.send({
    from: "Acme Billing <billing@example.com>",
    to: ["Jane Doe <jane@example.com>", "ops@example.com"],
    subject: "Invoice available",
    text: "Your June invoice is ready.",
});

console.log(mailer.getLastMessage()?.message.from);
// "Acme Billing <billing@example.com>"
console.log(result.accepted);
// ["Jane Doe <jane@example.com>", "ops@example.com"]

await mailer.shutdown();

Send HTML with a Plain-Text Fallback ​

Provide text and html together: capable clients render the HTML, while the text body serves as the fallback.

typescript
import { SmtpMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "localhost",
    port: 1025,
    secure: false,
});

const result = await mailer.send({
    from: "noreply@example.com",
    to: "customer@example.com",
    subject: "Your order shipped",
    text: "Order #1234 has shipped. Track it at https://example.com/track/1234",
    html: [
        "<h1>Your order shipped</h1>",
        "<p>Order <strong>#1234</strong> is on its way.</p>",
        '<p><a href="https://example.com/track/1234">Track your package</a></p>',
    ].join(""),
});

console.log("Accepted:", result.accepted); // ["customer@example.com"]

await mailer.shutdown();

Attach a File from Disk ​

Read a file into a Buffer and pass it as content with a contentType hint.

typescript
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { SmtpMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "smtp.example.com",
    port: 587,
    secure: false,
    auth: { user: "user@example.com", pass: "secret" },
});

const invoice = await readFile("./invoices/invoice-1042.pdf");

const result = await mailer.send({
    from: "billing@example.com",
    to: "customer@example.com",
    subject: "Invoice 1042",
    text: "Your invoice is attached.",
    attachments: [
        {
            filename: "invoice-1042.pdf",
            content: invoice, // Buffer straight from readFile
            contentType: "application/pdf",
        },
    ],
});

console.log("Accepted:", result.accepted); // ["customer@example.com"]

await mailer.shutdown();

Attach Base64-Encoded Content ​

content also accepts a base64-encoded string — convenient when the data comes from an API or database column.

typescript
import { MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();

const csv = "region,revenue\nEMEA,42000\nAPAC,31000";
const encoded = Buffer.from(csv, "utf-8").toString("base64");

await mailer.send({
    from: "reports@example.com",
    to: "management@example.com",
    subject: "Quarterly report",
    text: "The report is attached.",
    attachments: [
        {
            filename: "report.csv",
            content: encoded, // base64-encoded string
            contentType: "text/csv",
        },
    ],
});

const attachment = mailer.getLastMessage()?.message.attachments?.[0];
console.log(attachment?.filename); // "report.csv"
console.log(attachment?.contentType); // "text/csv"

await mailer.shutdown();

WebAFX Plugin Integration ​

Adapt any provider into a PluginDefinition. Creating and inspecting plugins is fully standalone; actual app.use() registration requires a WebAFX application context and is shown as a fragment.

Wrap an Existing Provider with createMailPlugin ​

createMailPlugin() wires any MailProvider — including custom subclasses — into WebAFX: singleton service registration, health hook, and shutdown hook.

typescript
import { createMailPlugin, MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

// Own the provider yourself so you can keep asserting on it in tests.
const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider({ serviceName: "mailer" });

const plugin = createMailPlugin(mailer);

console.log(plugin.name);           // "mailer" — taken from provider.serviceName
console.log(plugin.priority);       // 30 — default plugin priority
console.log(typeof plugin.factory); // "function" — invoked by WebAFX at bootstrap

// When WebAFX runs the factory it registers the provider as a singleton
// service and wires health()/shutdown() into the application lifecycle.

await mailer.shutdown();

One-Liner Memory Plugin ​

memoryMailPlugin() creates the MemoryMailProvider internally and returns a ready-to-use plugin.

typescript
import { memoryMailPlugin } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const plugin = memoryMailPlugin();

console.log(plugin.name);     // "mailer"
console.log(plugin.priority); // 30

const namedPlugin = memoryMailPlugin({ serviceName: "dev-mailer" });
console.log(namedPlugin.name); // "dev-mailer"

One-Liner SMTP Plugin ​

smtpMailPlugin(config) builds the SMTP provider from the config and wraps it in one call.

typescript
import { smtpMailPlugin } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const plugin = smtpMailPlugin({
    host: "smtp.example.com",
    port: 587,
    secure: false,
    auth: { user: "user@example.com", pass: "secret" },
});

console.log(plugin.name);           // "mailer"
console.log(plugin.priority);       // 30
console.log(typeof plugin.factory); // "function"

Register a Plugin in a WebAFX Application ​

Illustrative fragment — app and services are provided by the surrounding WebAFX application. The plugin registers the provider as a singleton under its service name; resolve it later with services.get<MailProvider>("mailer").

typescript
import { memoryMailPlugin, type MailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

// WebAFX application bootstrap
app.use(memoryMailPlugin());

// Anywhere in the application — resolve the registered singleton service:
const mailer = services.get<MailProvider>("mailer");

const result = await mailer.send({
    from: "noreply@example.com",
    to: "user@example.com",
    subject: "Welcome!",
    text: "Welcome to our service!",
});

console.log(result.accepted); // ["user@example.com"]

Configure Plugin Priority ​

Plugins default to priority 30; lower values install earlier. Pass { priority } as the second argument to createMailPlugin(). 0 is a valid priority.

typescript
import { createMailPlugin, MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();

console.log(createMailPlugin(mailer).priority);                  // 30 (default)
console.log(createMailPlugin(mailer, { priority: 5 }).priority); // 5
console.log(createMailPlugin(mailer, { priority: 0 }).priority); // 0 is valid

await mailer.shutdown();

Register Multiple Mailers Under Distinct Service Names ​

Because the plugin name equals the service name, several providers can coexist in one application.

typescript
import {
    createMailPlugin,
    MemoryMailProvider,
    SmtpMailProvider,
} from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const transactionalMailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "smtp.example.com",
    port: 587,
    secure: false,
    auth: { user: "user@example.com", pass: "secret" },
    serviceName: "transactional-mailer",
});

const marketingMailer = new MemoryMailProvider({ serviceName: "marketing-mailer" });

const transactionalPlugin = createMailPlugin(transactionalMailer);
const marketingPlugin = createMailPlugin(marketingMailer);

console.log(transactionalPlugin.name); // "transactional-mailer"
console.log(marketingPlugin.name);     // "marketing-mailer"

// In a WebAFX app: register both, then resolve by name:
// app.use(transactionalPlugin);
// app.use(marketingPlugin);

await transactionalMailer.shutdown();
await marketingMailer.shutdown();

Configuration and Backend Switching ​

Switch Backends per Environment with createMailProvider ​

createMailProvider() reads the type discriminator ("smtp" | "memory") and returns the matching provider — production can use SMTP while development and CI use memory, with no other code changes.

typescript
import {
    createMailPlugin,
    createMailProvider,
    type MailFactoryConfig,
    type MailProvider,
} from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

const isProduction = process.env.NODE_ENV === "production";

const config: MailFactoryConfig = {
    type: isProduction ? "smtp" : "memory",
    serviceName: isProduction ? "transactional-mailer" : "dev-mailer",
    host: process.env.SMTP_HOST ?? "localhost",
    port: Number(process.env.SMTP_PORT ?? "587"),
    secure: false,
    auth: process.env.SMTP_USER
        ? { user: process.env.SMTP_USER, pass: process.env.SMTP_PASS ?? "" }
        : undefined,
};

const mailer: MailProvider = createMailProvider(config);

console.log(mailer.serviceName);    // "dev-mailer" unless NODE_ENV === "production"
console.log(await mailer.health()); // true for the memory backend

// Wrap the selected provider as a WebAFX plugin.
const plugin = createMailPlugin(mailer);
console.log(plugin.name); // matches mailer.serviceName

await mailer.shutdown();

Note: when type can evaluate to "smtp", always supply host and port — the factory forwards them straight to the nodemailer transport.

Set a Custom Service Name ​

The default service name is exported as DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME ("mailer"); override it per provider for multi-mailer setups.

typescript
import { DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME, MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

console.log(DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME); // "mailer"

const defaultMailer = new MemoryMailProvider();
console.log(defaultMailer.serviceName); // "mailer"

const namedMailer = new MemoryMailProvider({ serviceName: "notifications-mailer" });
console.log(namedMailer.serviceName);   // "notifications-mailer"

await defaultMailer.shutdown();
await namedMailer.shutdown();

Handle Unknown Backend Types ​

The factory validates type at runtime and throws a descriptive error — useful when the value comes from an environment variable that TypeScript cannot check.

typescript
import { createMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

// Simulate an untyped value (e.g. from an environment variable).
const typeFromEnv: string = "sendgrid";

try {
    createMailProvider({ type: typeFromEnv as "smtp" });
} catch (error) {
    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    console.log(reason);
    // Unknown mail type: "sendgrid". Supported types: "smtp", "memory".
}

Testing Email Flows ​

The memory backend is purpose-built for tests: assert on getSentMessages() / getLastMessage() instead of hitting a real server.

Test a Password Reset Email ​

A complete Vitest suite using MemoryMailProvider with lifecycle cleanup in afterEach.

typescript
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { MemoryMailProvider, type MailMessage } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

describe("password reset flow", () => {
    let mailer: MemoryMailProvider;

    beforeEach(() => {
        mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();
    });

    afterEach(async () => {
        await mailer.shutdown();
    });

    it("sends the reset link to the user", async () => {
        const message: MailMessage = {
            from: "noreply@example.com",
            to: "user@example.com",
            subject: "Reset your password",
            text: "Open https://example.com/reset?token=abc123 to set a new password.",
        };

        const result = await mailer.send(message);

        expect(result.accepted).toEqual(["user@example.com"]);
        expect(result.rejected).toEqual([]);

        const last = mailer.getLastMessage();
        expect(last?.message.subject).toBe("Reset your password");
        expect(last?.message.text).toContain("token=abc123");
    });
});

Assert All Recipient Types Are Accepted ​

The memory backend flattens to + cc + bcc into accepted and always reports rejected: [], with message IDs following the <memory-…@test> pattern.

typescript
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

describe("notification fan-out", () => {
    let mailer: MemoryMailProvider;

    beforeEach(() => {
        mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();
    });

    afterEach(async () => {
        await mailer.shutdown();
    });

    it("accepts every to, cc, and bcc recipient", async () => {
        const result = await mailer.send({
            from: "alerts@example.com",
            to: ["oncall@example.com", "sre@example.com"],
            cc: "lead@example.com",
            bcc: "archive@example.com",
            subject: "Service degraded",
            text: "Elevated error rate detected.",
        });

        expect(result.accepted).toEqual([
            "oncall@example.com",
            "sre@example.com",
            "lead@example.com",
            "archive@example.com",
        ]);
        expect(result.rejected).toEqual([]);
        expect(result.messageId).toMatch(/^<memory-\d+-\d+@test>$/);
    });
});

Isolate Tests with clear() and shutdown() ​

shutdown() clears the store, so calling it in afterEach guarantees a clean slate; clear() resets state mid-test without recreating the provider.

typescript
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { MemoryMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

describe("mail store isolation", () => {
    let mailer: MemoryMailProvider;

    beforeEach(() => {
        mailer = new MemoryMailProvider();
    });

    afterEach(async () => {
        await mailer.shutdown(); // clears the store as well
    });

    it("records only the email sent inside this test", async () => {
        expect(mailer.getSentMessages()).toHaveLength(0);

        await mailer.send({
            from: "a@example.com",
            to: "b@example.com",
            subject: "First",
            text: "Body",
        });

        expect(mailer.getSentMessages()).toHaveLength(1);

        // Reset mid-test without recreating the provider.
        mailer.clear();
        expect(mailer.getSentMessages()).toHaveLength(0);
        expect(mailer.getLastMessage()).toBeUndefined();
    });
});

Custom Providers and Lifecycle ​

Implement a Custom MailProvider ​

Any delivery mechanism can be plugged in by subclassing MailProvider — here, a provider that persists emails as JSON files on disk. Custom providers also work with createMailPlugin().

typescript
import { mkdir, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { join } from "node:path";
import {
    MailProvider,
    type MailMessage,
    type MailProviderConfig,
    type MailResult,
} from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

/**
 * A custom MailProvider that persists emails as JSON files on disk.
 * Handy for local development when no SMTP server is running.
 */
class FileMailProvider extends MailProvider {
    private readonly outputDir: string;

    constructor(outputDir: string, config: MailProviderConfig = {}) {
        super(config);
        this.outputDir = outputDir;
    }

    async send(message: MailMessage): Promise<MailResult> {
        await mkdir(this.outputDir, { recursive: true });

        const safeSubject = message.subject.replace(/\W+/g, "-");
        const filename = `${Date.now()}-${safeSubject}.json`;
        await writeFile(
            join(this.outputDir, filename),
            JSON.stringify(message, null, 2),
            "utf-8"
        );

        const recipients = Array.isArray(message.to) ? message.to : [message.to];

        return {
            accepted: recipients,
            rejected: [],
            messageId: `<file-${filename}@local>`,
        };
    }

    async health(): Promise<boolean> {
        try {
            await mkdir(this.outputDir, { recursive: true });
            return true;
        } catch {
            return false;
        }
    }

    async shutdown(): Promise<void> {
        // Each send writes and closes its own file — nothing to release.
    }
}

const mailer = new FileMailProvider("./outbox", { serviceName: "file-mailer" });

console.log(mailer.serviceName); // "file-mailer"

const result = await mailer.send({
    from: "noreply@example.com",
    to: "dev@example.com",
    subject: "Local test",
    text: "Written to the outbox directory.",
});

console.log(result.accepted);       // ["dev@example.com"]
console.log(result.messageId);      // "<file-<filename>@local>"
console.log(await mailer.health()); // true

await mailer.shutdown();

Check Backend Health ​

health() verifies the SMTP connection with an EHLO/HELO handshake (no email sent) and returns false instead of throwing when the server is unreachable; the memory backend is always healthy.

typescript
import { MemoryMailProvider, SmtpMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

// Memory backend — no external dependencies, always healthy.
const memoryMailer = new MemoryMailProvider();
console.log(await memoryMailer.health()); // true

// SMTP backend — verify() checks the connection without sending mail.
const smtpMailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "localhost",
    port: 1025,
    secure: false,
});

console.log(await smtpMailer.health()); // true when an SMTP server listens on port 1025

// Unreachable server — health() reports false instead of throwing.
const unreachableMailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "localhost",
    port: 19999,
    secure: false,
});

console.log(await unreachableMailer.health()); // false

await memoryMailer.shutdown();
await smtpMailer.shutdown();
await unreachableMailer.shutdown();

Shut Down Gracefully ​

shutdown() clears the memory store or closes the SMTP connection pool. In a WebAFX app the plugin wires this into graceful disposal automatically.

typescript
import { MemoryMailProvider, SmtpMailProvider } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

// --- Memory backend: shutdown() clears the message store ---------------
const memoryMailer = new MemoryMailProvider();

await memoryMailer.send({
    from: "a@example.com",
    to: "b@example.com",
    subject: "Stored",
    text: "Stored in memory.",
});

console.log(memoryMailer.getSentMessages().length); // 1

await memoryMailer.shutdown();

console.log(memoryMailer.getSentMessages().length); // 0

// --- SMTP backend: shutdown() closes the connection pool ---------------
const smtpMailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "smtp.example.com",
    port: 587,
    secure: false,
    auth: { user: "user@example.com", pass: "secret" },
});

// While the transport is open, send() delivers messages. After shutdown(),
// the pool is closed and any further send() call fails — so call it last.
await smtpMailer.shutdown();

Handle SMTP Send Failures ​

Connection errors, authentication failures, and send rejections are thrown from send() — wrap sends in try/catch and always close the transport in finally.

typescript
import { SmtpMailProvider, type MailMessage } from "blendsdk/webafx-mailer";

// Point at a port where nothing is listening to trigger a connection failure.
const mailer = new SmtpMailProvider({
    host: "localhost",
    port: 19999,
    secure: false,
});

const message: MailMessage = {
    from: "noreply@example.com",
    to: "customer@example.com",
    subject: "Order confirmation",
    text: "Your order is confirmed.",
};

try {
    const result = await mailer.send(message);
    console.log("Accepted:", result.accepted);
} catch (error) {
    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    console.error("Email delivery failed:", reason);
    // Typical output: Email delivery failed: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:19999
} finally {
    await mailer.shutdown();
}
